thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1954123456 — Reserved GPU pool 'reserved-pool-7' crossing 95% utilization and pending-queue growing. Autoscaler failing to launch new nodes (quota_exceeded). Paging on-call SREs: @sre-jen @ops-night-raj

sre-jen: I'm taking this. Saw sudden jump in pending requests ~00:02 UTC. Dashboard shows sustained 5k+ queued tokens and 98% GPU allocation in pool-7.

eng-miguel: ping — infra team here. autoscaler logs show repeated 403 from cloud API: 
```
2026-03-15T00:01:42Z autoscaler: create_node failed: quota_exceeded: GPU quota 0 of 2 remaining
```
Looks like region quota hit + rate-limits on node creation.

platops-sam: also seeing noisy neighbor behavior — one enterprise tenant (acct: acme-corp) has a surge of long-running parallel jobs on standard reservations. Their pods pinned to all GPUs. Other reserved workloads are starving.

cs-aly: Customer impact: ACME and two other enterprise tenants reporting timeouts and throttled predictions. CS received 3 escalations in last 8 mins.

sre-jen: Ok. Immediate mitigation options: 1) manual eviction of noisy pods, 2) throttle ACME's concurrency via rate-limit policy, 3) temporarily migrate lower-priority tenants to fallback model variant (smaller) or to hosted fallback. Which is fastest?

eng-miguel: fastest is manual eviction + apply a network-level rate-limit for ACME. I'll prepare patch for the admission controller to set concurrency to 2 for that namespace.

platops-sam: I can run a safe eviction sweep for pods with label `job=ad-hoc-batch` in reserved-pool-7. That will free GPUs immediately but will cause their jobs to fail — need CS signoff.

cs-aly: We prefer not to drop customer jobs without notice. Can we pause new ACME jobs instead and throttle existing ones? I'll reach out to their engineering contact.

ops-night-raj: If quota is the blocker for new nodes, we should also try to provision in a neighboring region temporarily and failover routing for low-latency tolerant tenants. That takes ~10-15m to warm.

sre-jen: Actions I am executing now:
- add emergency rate-limit on ACME namespace (concurrency -> 2)
- start manual eviction of top 3 noisy deployments with `job=ad-hoc-batch` but mark as 'soft-evict' (send SIGTERM + 30s grace)
- cold-start fallback route for non-enterprise tenants to hosted models

Command snippets I'm running:
```
# set quota override (temporary) for acme namespace
kubectl annotate ns acme-corp redwood.io/emergency-concurrency=2 --overwrite

# list top GPU consumers
kubectl top pods -n reserved-pool-7 --sort-by=cpu | head -n 10

# soft-evict candidate pods
kubectl -n reserved-pool-7 get pods -l job=ad-hoc-batch -o name | xargs -r -n1 kubectl -n reserved-pool-7 delete --grace-period=30
```

infra-bot: autoscaler: attempted node creations: 18 in last 3m; cloud API returned quota_exceeded for region us-west-2; failover possible to us-west-1. Suggested action: request temporary quota bump or fallback region.

eng-miguel: I've submitted emergency request to cloud quota team (ticket #CLOUD-8742) and opened a programmatic failover flag to allow us-west-1 provisioning.

platops-sam: Evictions started — freed 4 GPUs so far. Pending queue dropped from 5.2k -> 3.1k. Latency for affected tenants improving but still above SLO.

cs-aly: ACME contact answered — they confirmed a scheduled batch ramp that wasn't gated. They asked for a pause rather than kills. I told them we're throttling concurrency by 2 and asked them to backfill via smaller batches. They acknowledged.

sre-jen: Rolling canary to migrate non-critical tenants to fallback hosted endpoint now. If CPU/GPU pressure persists we'll escalate to manual eviction of longer-running ACME jobs.

ops-night-raj: us-west-1 provisioning is in progress; expecting nodes in ~12m. If nodes come up, we should rebalance pods rather than evict further.

platops-sam: Note — evicting the noisy pods caused a few job failures; logged incident IDs to track. We insulated enterprise reserved tenants with higher-priority QoS but the noisy jobs were marked as guaranteed and still starved others due to placement constraints. Need longer-term policy change.

sre-jen: Current status update at T+20m: queued requests 800 -> 1.2k (peak was 5.2k), reserved-pool-7 GPU utilization 83%, ACME concurrency reduced. Cloud quota still pending. Partial mitigation good.

cs-aly: Sending an interim customer communication to affected tenants: short explanation, immediate mitigations, ETA for full recovery (~45m). Will copy SRE notes.

eng-miguel: Follow-up tasks I'm creating: (1) enforce namespace-level burst limits for reserved pools, (2) add autoscaler telemetry alert for repeated quota_exceeded errors, (3) improve scheduler to avoid over-pinning guaranteed pods.

sre-jen: Final actions for oncall handoff to day team: document steps taken, keep ACME concurrency at 2 until quota bump or failover verified, monitor queue and latency. Handoff to @eng-miguel and @platops-sam in morning.

ops-night-raj: Leaving oncall. Leaving note: watch for slow drain when new nodes come up — rebalance gently, don't mass-evict.

on-thread followups (to create JIRA):
- RED-INC-2026: Emergency eviction audit & customer job replay support
- RED-OPS-2026: Quota fallback automation (multi-region)
- RED-SRE-2026: Namespace burst policy for reserved pools

sre-jen: Closing pager at T+55m. Postmortem will include timeline, customer impact, and a proposed change to reserved pool admission controller. Thanks everyone. :heart:

cs-aly: I'll follow up with affected accounts and share the CS template once done.

platops-sam: leaving final logs & commands in incident wiki.

eng-miguel: created follow-up PR for admission controller default concurrency. link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4398

on-thread note: severity downgraded to P2 after queue stabilized and ACME agreed to pause ramp.
